"""Launch the bundled Miles fully-async GRPO trainer on the public workload.

Topology, model and rollout settings live in ``scripts/run_config.json``; this
file only turns them into the Miles command line, starts any local services the
rollout needs, and records the exact launch in ``experiment_logs/<run>/``.

    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py                 # full run
    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py --print-command # show the trainer argv
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def model_args(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Megatron shape arguments, derived from the HF config of the prepared model."""
    hf = json.loads((WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"] / "config.json").read_text())
    text = hf.get("text_config", hf)
    args = [
        "--spec", "miles_plugins.models.qwen3_5", "get_qwen3_5_spec",
        "--disable-bias-linear", "--qk-layernorm", "--group-query-attention",
        "--num-attention-heads", str(text["num_attention_heads"]),
        "--num-query-groups", str(text["num_key_value_heads"]),
        "--kv-channels", str(text["head_dim"]),
        "--num-layers", str(text["num_hidden_layers"]),
        "--hidden-size", str(text["hidden_size"]),
        "--normalization", "RMSNorm", "--apply-layernorm-1p", "--position-embedding-type", "rope",
        "--norm-epsilon", str(text.get("rms_norm_eps", 1e-6)),
        "--rotary-percent", str(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("partial_rotary_factor", 0.25)),
        "--rotary-base", str(int(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("rope_theta", 10_000_000))),
        "--swiglu", "--untie-embeddings-and-output-weights", "--vocab-size", str(text["vocab_size"]),
        "--attention-output-gate",
    ]
    if text.get("num_experts"):
        layers = text["num_hidden_layers"]
        args += [
            "--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-shared-expert-intermediate-size", str(text["shared_expert_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-router-score-function", "softmax", "--moe-router-topk", str(text["num_experts_per_tok"]),
            "--moe-layer-freq", f"[1]*{layers}", "--num-experts", str(text["num_experts"]),
            "--moe-grouped-gemm", "--moe-token-drop-policy", "probs", "--moe-router-dtype", "fp32",
            "--moe-permute-fusion", "--moe-aux-loss-coeff", "0", "--moe-shared-expert-gate",
            "--moe-token-dispatcher-type", "alltoall",
        ]
    else:
        args += ["--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["intermediate_size"])]
    return args


def torch_dist_dir(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return WORKSPACE / (cfg["model"]["path"] + "_torch_dist")


def convert_checkpoint(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> None:
    """One-time HF -> Megatron torch_dist conversion (offline, on the task GPUs)."""
    target = torch_dist_dir(cfg)
    if (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        return
    conv = cfg["conversion"]
    argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc-per-node", str(conv["gpus"]),
            "scripts/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py", *model_args(cfg),
            # Shard the conversion by pipeline stage, never by expert: mbridge's loader for the
            # fused 3-D expert tensors of the public checkpoint ignores the expert-parallel offset,
            # so with EP>1 every rank would load experts 0..E/EP-1. Training reshards on load.
            "--tensor-model-parallel-size", "1", "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", str(conv["pp"]),
            "--expert-model-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
            "--seq-length", "4096", "--max-position-embeddings", "4096", "--bf16",
            "--rollout-batch-size", "1",  # required by the Miles argument set; unused here
            "--hf-checkpoint", str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"]), "--save", str(target)]
    (log_dir / "convert_command.json").write_text(json.dumps(argv, indent=2) + "\n")
    with open(log_dir / "convert.log", "ab") as log:
        rc = subprocess.call(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if rc != 0 or not (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        raise RuntimeError(f"checkpoint conversion failed (exit {rc}); see {log_dir / 'convert.log'}")


def build_command(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    topo, roll, train, router = cfg["topology"], cfg["rollout"], cfg["training"], cfg["router"]
    model = str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"])
    argv = [
        sys.executable, "scripts/native_entrypoint.py",
        "--train-backend", "megatron",
        "--actor-num-nodes", "1", "--actor-num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus", str(topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus-per-engine", str(topo["rollout_gpus_per_engine"]),
        "--num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"] + topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--hf-checkpoint", model, "--ref-load", str(torch_dist_dir(cfg)), "--bf16",
        *model_args(cfg),
        "--seq-length", str(roll["max_context_len"]), "--max-position-embeddings", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--tensor-model-parallel-size", str(train["tp"]), "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", "1",
        "--context-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-model-parallel-size", str(train["ep"]),
        "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
        "--recompute-granularity", "full", "--recompute-method", "uniform", "--recompute-num-layers", "1",
        "--use-dynamic-batch-size", "--max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        # 248k-entry vocabulary: never materialize [tokens, vocab] logits
        "--fused-logprob", "--log-probs-max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["log_probs_max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        "--advantage-estimator", "grpo", "--entropy-coef", "0", "--eps-clip", "0.2", "--eps-clip-high", "0.28",
        "--optimizer", "adam", "--lr", str(train["lr"]), "--lr-decay-style", "constant",
        "--weight-decay", "0.1", "--adam-beta1", "0.9", "--adam-beta2", "0.98",
        "--attention-dropout", "0.0", "--hidden-dropout", "0.0",
        "--attention-softmax-in-fp32", "--attention-backend", "flash",
        "--rollout-function-path", "runtime.rollout.generate_rollout",
        "--custom-generate-function-path", "runtime.agent_generate.generate",
        # Generate-function options reach the legacy rollout path through Miles'
        # --custom-config-path YAML (written next to the run logs by main()).
        "--custom-config-path", "{custom_config}",
        "--prompt-data", str(WORKSPACE / roll["data"]), "--input-key", "messages", "--label-key", "label",
        "--metadata-key", "metadata", "--rollout-shuffle", "--rollout-seed", "20261116",
        "--num-rollout", str(roll["num_rollout"]), "--rollout-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"]),
        "--n-samples-per-prompt", str(roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--global-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"] * roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--rollout-max-response-len", str(roll["max_new_tokens_per_turn"]),
        "--rollout-max-context-len", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--rollout-temperature", "1.0", "--rollout-top-p", "1.0",
        "--sglang-mem-fraction-static", str(roll["sglang_mem_fraction"]),
        "--sglang-server-concurrency", str(roll["server_concurrency"]),
        "--update-weights-interval", "1", "--pause-generation-mode", "abort",
        "--custom-megatron-before-train-step-hook-path", "runtime.training_evidence.observe_train_step",
        "--no-use-prometheus-scrape",
    ]
    if train.get("fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"):
        argv += ["--fused-logprob-seq-chunk-size", str(train["fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"])]
    if train.get("grads_in_fp32", True):
        argv += ["--accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32"]
    if train.get("optimizer_cpu_offload"):
        argv += ["--optimizer-cpu-offload", "--use-precision-aware-optimizer"]
        if train.get("overlap_cpu_optimizer_transfers", False):
            argv += ["--overlap-cpu-optimizer-d2h-h2d"]
    if train["tp"] > 1:
        argv += ["--sequence-parallel"]
    if router.get("use_miles_router"):
        argv += ["--use-miles-router"]
    if router.get("policy"):
        argv += ["--sglang-router-policy", router["policy"]]
    return argv + cfg.get("extra_args", [])


def start_services(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> list[subprocess.Popen]:
    procs = []
    for svc in cfg.get("services", []):
        cmd = [sys.executable, *[a.replace("{log_dir}", str(log_dir)) for a in svc["argv"]]]
        out = open(log_dir / f"{svc['name']}.log", "ab")
        procs.append(subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT))
        url = svc.get("health_url")
        for _ in range(120):
            if url is None:
                break
            try:
                import urllib.request

                # local service: never route the probe through a host proxy
                urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({})).open(url, timeout=2)
                break
            except Exception:
                time.sleep(0.5)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"service {svc['name']} did not become healthy")
    return procs


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--print-command", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, default=WORKSPACE / "scripts/run_config.json")
    options, extra = parser.parse_known_args()
    cfg = json.loads(options.config.read_text())
    argv = build_command(cfg) + extra
    if options.print_command:
        print(shlex.join(argv))
        return 0
    run_name = time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime()) + f"-{os.getpid()}"
    # The harness collects $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs; a manual launch logs into the workspace.
    log_root = Path(os.environ["AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS"]) if os.environ.get("AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS") else WORKSPACE
    log_dir = log_root / "experiment_logs" / run_name
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    custom_config = log_dir / "generate_args.yaml"
    custom_config.write_text(json.dumps({

Now we're getting somewhere:

- 662 env setups, but only 543 done + 29 engine_abort = 572 trajectory sessions that got to generation? Actually 660 sessions had generate calls. 662 env setups for 660 sessions (some retried).
- 678 sandbox creates, but only 547 deletes → 131 leaked sandboxes at end. That's a resource leak. `live` reaches 131 at end. This could be a root cause: sandbox service has a concurrency limit (e.g., max live sandboxes or provisioning limit 19). The semaphore waits are huge: p50 35.5s, p90 114.7s, max 160s. Sandbox creates p50 7.25s, but env_setup create_s p50 18.8s (queueing inside service?).
- 662 env setups for 3 rollouts × 16 groups × 8 = 384 expected trajectories. But 662 > 384. Because the producer runs ahead (32 groups in-flight; 2 batches ahead), so it creates sandboxes for future rollouts too. At the end, 131 sandboxes leaked because the producer was stopped mid-generation and cleanup didn't finish? The log said "Closing loop with 1 generation tasks still cancelling" and "drained 15 completed". There were 32 active tasks when stopping; only some canceled. 131 leaked is a big number though.

Hmm, wait: 678 creates - 547 deletes = 131. Also maybe delete failures or sessions still alive. Could be the sandbox service holds max live limit? `max live 159` - wow. That's a lot of sandboxes for 8 samples × 32 inflight = 256 possible.

What's the sandbox_service's concurrency? Let's read runtime/sandbox_service.py and vendor/agent_runtime/env_runtime.py to see semaphore semantics. The log line "sandbox setup waited X s for semaphore" is in env_runtime.py, client-side. Maybe there's a client-side semaphore with a small limit (e.g., 8 or 16), causing serialization: 662 setups each ~20s create + semaphore wait; total rollout 0 234s. Historical had p50 190s waits. Maybe the semaphore limit is a config knob (SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT?) that is too low, or it's hard-coded.

Actually wait. There's something even more suspicious: 662 env setups > 384 training trajectories. The producer fetched 95 groups before rollout 2: 95×8 = 760 potential trajectories; but only 662 env sets and 543 done. So many trajectories were generated but never consumed (backend prefetch). That's expected with async worker running ahead by up to 32 groups (256 trajectories). But by run end, the producer was stopped with 15 completed groups drained (i.e., 120 samples discarded) plus 1 task still cancelling. That's wasted work but not a training bug.

Now, is the health issue maybe that training throughput is dominated by sandbox setup latency? The rollouts take 234s/77s and training steps 256s/42s/38s. With only 3 steps, total run 14 min. Hmm.

But the task says "determine whether the training setup is healthy". Maybe it's not, due to a specific bug: The env_setup `create_s` p50 18.8s vs sandbox service create p50 7.25s. Why the discrepancy? Because create_s in env_setup measures client-observed time including waiting for service? Let's read env_runtime.py.

Also interesting: 678 creates, 669 uploads, 665 installs, so 9 creates without upload, etc. And 547 deletes → 131 leaked. If the sandbox service has a cap on live sandboxes (e.g., 160?), we saw live 159 max. Maybe a hard limit 160; if reached, creates block? Let's read sandbox_service.py.

1	"""Local sandbox control plane used by the public rollout.
2	
3	The service models the remote sandbox provider the original run used: creating
4	a sandbox, uploading the repository, installing tool commands, executing tool
5	calls and deleting the sandbox are separate HTTP operations with their own
6	latency.  Provisioning slows down as more sandboxes are being created at once,
7	which is how the hosted provider behaved under burst load.  All latencies come
8	from a seeded generator and every request is appended to a JSONL access log.
9	"""
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import argparse
13	import asyncio
14	import itertools
15	import json
16	import os
17	import random
18	import sys
19	import time
20	from pathlib import Path
21	
22	from aiohttp import web
23	
24	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
25	from runtime import repo_tools  # noqa: E402
26	
27	
28	class SandboxService:
29	    def __init__(self, options):
30	        self.options = options
31	        self.rng = random.Random(options.seed)
32	        self.ids = itertools.count(1)
33	        self.sandboxes: dict[str, dict] = {}
34	        self.provisioning = 0
35	        self.counters = {"created": 0, "deleted": 0, "exec": 0, "uploads": 0, "installs": 0}
36	        self.log = open(options.access_log, "a", buffering=1, encoding="utf-8")
37	
38	    def _record(self, op: str, started: float, **extra) -> None:
39	        self.log.write(json.dumps({"op": op, "t": started, "duration_s": round(time.time() - started, 4),
40	                                   "live": len(self.sandboxes), "provisioning": self.provisioning, **extra}) + "\n")
41	
42	    def _latency(self, median: float) -> float:
43	        return median * self.rng.lognormvariate(0.0, self.options.sigma)
44	
45	    async def create(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
46	        started = time.time()
47	        body = await request.json()
48	        self.provisioning += 1
49	        try:
50	            contention = 1.0 + self.provisioning / self.options.provider_capacity
51	            await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.create_s) * contention)
52	        finally:
53	            self.provisioning -= 1
54	        sandbox_id = f"sbx-{next(self.ids):06d}"
55	        self.sandboxes[sandbox_id] = {"template": body.get("template"), "files": {}, "test_failure": "", "commands": False}
56	        self.counters["created"] += 1
57	        self._record("create", started, sandbox=sandbox_id)
58	        return web.json_response({"sandbox_id": sandbox_id, "status": "running"})
59

"""Local sandbox control plane used by the public rollout.

The service models the remote sandbox provider the original run used: creating
a sandbox, uploading the repository, installing tool commands, executing tool
calls and deleting the sandbox are separate HTTP operations with their own
latency.  Provisioning slows down as more sandboxes are being created at once,
which is how the hosted provider behaved under burst load.  All latencies come
from a seeded generator and every request is appended to a JSONL access log.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import itertools
import json
import os
import random
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from aiohttp import web

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from runtime import repo_tools  # noqa: E402


class SandboxService:
    def __init__(self, options):
        self.options = options
        self.rng = random.Random(options.seed)
        self.ids = itertools.count(1)
        self.sandboxes: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.provisioning = 0
        self.counters = {"created": 0, "deleted": 0, "exec": 0, "uploads": 0, "installs": 0}
        self.log = open(options.access_log, "a", buffering=1, encoding="utf-8")

    def _record(self, op: str, started: float, **extra) -> None:
        self.log.write(json.dumps({"op": op, "t": started, "duration_s": round(time.time() - started, 4),
                                   "live": len(self.sandboxes), "provisioning": self.provisioning, **extra}) + "\n")

    def _latency(self, median: float) -> float:
        return median * self.rng.lognormvariate(0.0, self.options.sigma)

    async def create(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        body = await request.json()
        self.provisioning += 1
        try:
            contention = 1.0 + self.provisioning / self.options.provider_capacity
            await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.create_s) * contention)
        finally:
            self.provisioning -= 1
        sandbox_id = f"sbx-{next(self.ids):06d}"
        self.sandboxes[sandbox_id] = {"template": body.get("template"), "files": {}, "test_failure": "", "commands": False}
        self.counters["created"] += 1
        self._record("create", started, sandbox=sandbox_id)
        return web.json_response({"sandbox_id": sandbox_id, "status": "running"})

    def _get(self, request: web.Request) -> dict:
        sandbox = self.sandboxes.get(request.match_info["sid"])
        if sandbox is None:
            raise web.HTTPNotFound(text="unknown sandbox")
        return sandbox

    async def upload(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        sandbox = self._get(request)
        body = await request.json()
        size = sum(len(v) for v in body.get("files", {}).values())
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.upload_s) * (1 + size / 200_000))
        sandbox["files"] = body.get("files", {})
        sandbox["test_failure"] = body.get("test_failure", "")
        self.counters["uploads"] += 1
        self._record("upload", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"], bytes=size)
        return web.json_response({"ok": True})

    async def install(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        sandbox = self._get(request)
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.install_s))
        sandbox["commands"] = True
        self.counters["installs"] += 1
        self._record("install", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"])
        return web.json_response({"ok": True})

    async def execute(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        sandbox = self._get(request)
        if not sandbox["commands"]:
            return web.json_response({"error": "tool commands are not installed"}, status=409)
        body = await request.json()
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.exec_s))
        output = repo_tools.execute(sandbox["files"], sandbox["test_failure"], body["tool"], body.get("params") or {})
        self.counters["exec"] += 1
        self._record("exec", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"], tool=body["tool"])
        return web.json_response({"output": output})

    async def delete(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        self.sandboxes.pop(request.match_info["sid"], None)
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.delete_s))
        self.counters["deleted"] += 1
        self._record("delete", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"])
        return web.json_response({"ok": True})

    async def stats(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        return web.json_response({"live": len(self.sandboxes), "provisioning": self.provisioning, **self.counters})


def build_app(options) -> web.Application:
    service = SandboxService(options)
    app = web.Application(client_max_size=64 * 1024 * 1024)
    app.add_routes([
        web.post("/sandboxes", service.create),
        web.post("/sandboxes/{sid}/files", service.upload),
        web.post("/sandboxes/{sid}/commands", service.install),
        web.post("/sandboxes/{sid}/exec", service.execute),
        web.delete("/sandboxes/{sid}", service.delete),
        web.get("/stats", service.stats),
        web.get("/health", lambda request: web.json_response({"ok": True})),
    ])
    return app


def parse_args(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("SANDBOX_SERVICE_PORT", "18080")))
    parser.add_argument("--access-log", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261110)
    parser.add_argument("--create-s", type=float, default=6.0)
    parser.add_argument("--upload-s", type=float, default=1.5)
    parser.add_argument("--install-s", type=float, default=2.0)
    parser.add_argument("--exec-s", type=float, default=0.4)
    parser.add_argument("--delete-s", type=float, default=0.3)
    parser.add_argument("--sigma", type=float, default=0.45)
    parser.add_argument("--provider-capacity", type=float, default=48.0)
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    opts = parse_args()
    opts.access_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    web.run_app(build_app(opts), host=opts.host, port=opts.port, access_log=None, print=None)

"""Build the public repository-debugging workload used by the rollout.

Every task is a small synthetic Python project with one planted defect and a
failing unit test.  The agent has to inspect the project through tools, so a
trajectory is a genuine multi-turn conversation whose context grows with every
file it reads.  The generator is deterministic: the same seed always yields the
same JSONL bytes, and `--check` compares them against the recorded digest.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path

DOMAINS = {
    "inventory": ("item", "stock", "warehouse", "reorder", "sku"),
    "billing": ("invoice", "charge", "customer", "refund", "ledger"),
    "scheduler": ("job", "slot", "worker", "deadline", "queue"),
    "telemetry": ("sample", "metric", "window", "bucket", "series"),
    "catalog": ("product", "price", "category", "discount", "listing"),
    "routing": ("route", "hop", "segment", "carrier", "zone"),
}
# Each defect: (correct expression, broken expression, failing behaviour).
DEFECTS = [
    ("total += value", "total -= value", "accumulates the wrong sign"),
    ("if count >= limit:", "if count > limit:", "misses the boundary value"),
    ("return values[: size]", "return values[: size - 1]", "drops the last element"),
    ("ratio = part / whole if whole else 0.0", "ratio = part / (whole + 1) if whole else 0.0", "skews the ratio"),
    ("key = name.strip().lower()", "key = name.strip()", "treats differently-cased names as distinct"),
    ("start = max(0, offset)", "start = offset", "accepts negative offsets"),
    ("best = min(candidates, key=cost)", "best = max(candidates, key=cost)", "selects the most expensive candidate"),
    ("window = items[index - span + 1 : index + 1]", "window = items[index - span : index]", "shifts the window by one"),
]
SYSTEM = (
    "You are a software engineer working in a sandboxed repository. Use the provided tools to "
    "inspect files and run the test-suite. When you have identified the defect, call submit_fix "
    "with the file path, the function name and a short explanation. Do not guess without reading code."
)


def _helper(rng: random.Random, noun: str, idx: int) -> str:
    verb = rng.choice(["normalize", "collect", "merge", "validate", "render", "index", "partition", "score"])
    lines = [
        f"def {verb}_{noun}_{idx}(records, *, strict=False):",
        f'    """{verb.capitalize()} {noun} records (helper #{idx})."""',
        "    out = []",
        "    for position, record in enumerate(records):",
        f"        if strict and not isinstance(record, dict):",
        f"            raise TypeError(f'{noun} record {{position}} must be a mapping')",
        f"        entry = dict(record)",
        f"        entry.setdefault('{noun}_id', position)",
        f"        entry['{verb}_done'] = True",
        "        out.append(entry)",
        "    return out",
        "",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _target(defect: tuple[str, str, str], noun: str, fname: str, broken: bool) -> str:
    good, bad, _ = defect
    line = bad if broken else good
    body = {
        0: [f"def {fname}(values):", "    total = 0", "    for value in values:", f"        {line}", "    return total"],
        1: [f"def {fname}(count, limit):", f"    {line}", "        return True", "    return False"],
        2: [f"def {fname}(values, size):", "    values = list(values)", f"    {line}"],
        3: [f"def {fname}(part, whole):", f"    {line}", "    return round(ratio, 6)"],
        4: [f"def {fname}(names):", "    seen = {}", "    for name in names:", f"        {line}", "        seen[key] = seen.get(key, 0) + 1", "    return seen"],
        5: [f"def {fname}(items, offset, size):", f"    {line}", "    return items[start : start + size]"],
        6: [f"def {fname}(candidates, cost):", "    if not candidates:", "        return None", f"    {line}", "    return best"],
        7: [f"def {fname}(items, index, span):", f"    {line}", "    return sum(window) / len(window)"],
    }[DEFECTS.index(defect)]
    doc = f'    """Core {noun} computation used by the public API."""'
    return "\n".join([body[0], doc, *body[1:], ""])


TESTS = {
    0: ("assert {f}([1, 2, 3]) == 6", "AssertionError: assert -6 == 6"),
    1: ("assert {f}(5, 5) is True", "AssertionError: assert False is True"),
    2: ("assert {f}([1, 2, 3], 3) == [1, 2, 3]", "AssertionError: assert [1, 2] == [1, 2, 3]"),
    3: ("assert {f}(1, 4) == 0.25", "AssertionError: assert 0.2 == 0.25"),
    4: ("assert {f}(['A', 'a']) == {{'a': 2}}", "AssertionError: assert {'A': 1, 'a': 1} == {'a': 2}"),
    5: ("assert {f}([1, 2, 3], -1, 2) == [1, 2]", "AssertionError: assert [] == [1, 2]"),
    6: ("assert {f}([3, 1, 2], cost=lambda x: x) == 1", "AssertionError: assert 3 == 1"),
    7: ("assert {f}([1, 2, 3, 4], 3, 2) == 3.5", "AssertionError: assert 2.5 == 3.5"),
}


def build_task(task_id: int, seed: int) -> dict:
    rng = random.Random(seed * 100003 + task_id)
    domain = rng.choice(sorted(DOMAINS))
    nouns = DOMAINS[domain]
    defect_index = rng.randrange(len(DEFECTS))
    defect = DEFECTS[defect_index]
    modules = rng.sample(["core", "models", "service", "storage", "utils", "reports", "api", "cache"], 6)
    target_module = rng.choice(modules)
    target_noun = rng.choice(nouns)
    target_fn = f"compute_{target_noun}_{rng.choice(['total', 'window', 'ratio', 'selection', 'keys', 'page', 'limit'])}"
    files: dict[str, str] = {}
    for module in modules:
        chunks = [f'"""{domain}.{module}: {module} helpers for {domain} records."""', "", "from __future__ import annotations", ""]
        for idx in range(rng.randint(5, 9)):
            chunks.append(_helper(rng, rng.choice(nouns), idx))
        if module == target_module:
            chunks.insert(rng.randint(4, len(chunks)), _target(defect, target_noun, target_fn, broken=True))
        else:
            decoy = f"compute_{rng.choice(nouns)}_{rng.choice(['summary', 'batch', 'view'])}"
            chunks.append(_target(rng.choice(DEFECTS), rng.choice(nouns), decoy, broken=False))
        files[f"{domain}/{module}.py"] = "\n".join(chunks)
    test_src, failure = TESTS[defect_index]
    files[f"tests/test_{target_module}.py"] = "\n".join([
        f"from {domain}.{target_module} import {target_fn}", "", "",
        f"def test_{target_fn}():", "    " + test_src.format(f=target_fn), "",
    ])
    files["README.md"] = f"# {domain}\n\nInternal {domain} toolkit. Run `pytest -q` to execute the test-suite.\n"
    path = f"{domain}/{target_module}.py"
    user = (f"The test-suite of the `{domain}` repository is failing. Find the defect that makes it fail. "
            f"Inspect the repository with the tools before answering, then call submit_fix.")
    return {
        "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
        "label": json.dumps({"path": path, "function": target_fn}, sort_keys=True),
        "metadata": {
            "task_id": f"repo-{task_id:04d}",
            "files": files,
            "test_failure": f"FAILED tests/test_{target_module}.py::test_{target_fn} - {failure}",
            "defect_class": defect[2],
        },
    }


def build(count: int, seed: int) -> bytes:
    rows = [json.dumps(build_task(i, seed), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) for i in range(count)]
    return ("\n".join(rows) + "\n").encode("utf-8")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261116)
    parser.add_argument("--sha256", default=None, help="expected digest of the generated JSONL")
    options = parser.parse_args()
    data = build(options.count, options.seed)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    if options.sha256 and digest != options.sha256:
        raise SystemExit(f"workload digest mismatch: {digest} != {options.sha256}")
    options.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    options.out.write_bytes(data)
    print(json.dumps({"tasks": options.count, "bytes": len(data), "sha256": digest, "path": str(options.out)}))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""
Simple multi-turn generation with tool calling.
"""

import argparse
import time
from copy import deepcopy

from miles.rollout.base_types import GenerateFnInput, GenerateFnOutput
from miles.rollout.generate_utils.generate_endpoint_utils import (
    compute_prompt_ids_from_sample,
    compute_request_payload,
    compute_routing_headers,
    update_sample_from_response,
)
from miles.rollout.generate_utils.tool_call_utils import (
    create_tool_call_parser,
    execute_tool_calls,
    update_sample_with_tool_responses,
)
from miles.utils.lifecycle import TrajectoryLifecycle
from miles.utils.misc import load_function


async def generate(input: GenerateFnInput) -> GenerateFnOutput:
    # ----------------------- Setup -------------------------

    args = input.args
    sample = deepcopy(input.sample)
    tokenizer = input.state.tokenizer
    assert not args.partial_rollout, "Partial rollout is not supported"

    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"

    execute_tool_function = load_function(args.generate_execute_tool_function_path)

    tool_specs = load_function(args.generate_tool_specs_path)
    tool_call_parser = create_tool_call_parser(tool_specs, args.generate_tool_call_parser)

    # tool-call markup stays inline in the assistant text (what the model emitted)
    record_trajectory = args.save_debug_trajectory_data is not None
    trajectory = (list(sample.prompt) if isinstance(sample.prompt, list) else []) if record_trajectory else None

import logging
from argparse import Namespace
from math import isclose

import numpy as np
import psutil
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from miles.utils import train_metric_utils
from miles.utils.flops_utils import calculate_fwd_flops
from miles.utils.ft_utils.process_group_utils import MultiPGUtil
from miles.utils.metric_utils import compute_rollout_step
from miles.utils.tracking_utils.structured_log import log_structured
from miles.utils.types import RolloutBatch

from ...utils.tracking_utils import tracking
from .cp_utils import get_sum_of_sample_mean
from .data import DataIterator
from .parallel import get_parallel_state

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def gather_log_data(
    metric_name: str,
    args: Namespace,
    rollout_id: int,
    log_dict: dict[str, float],
) -> dict[str, float] | None:
    """
    Gather per-rank metrics, reduce by mean on the DP source rank, and log.

    Expects `log_dict` to contain plain scalars. The DP source rank prints and
    optionally logs to WandB/TensorBoard with a step derived from `rollout_id` and
    batch sizes. Returns the reduced dict on the DP source rank; returns None on others.
    """

    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()

    pg = parallel_state.effective_dp_cp
    log_structured(logger.info, op="cross_cell", phase="start", kind="log_gather", rank=pg.rank)
    try:
        gathered_log_dict = MultiPGUtil.gather_object(
            obj=log_dict,
            groups_inner_to_outer=pg.gloo_groups_inner_to_outer,
        )
        log_structured(logger.info, op="cross_cell", phase="end", kind="log_gather", rank=pg.rank, success=True)
    except RuntimeError:
        log_structured(
            logger.warning,
            op="cross_cell",
            phase="end",
            kind="log_gather",
            rank=pg.rank,
            success=False,
            degraded=True,
            exc_info=True,
        )
        return None

    if pg.rank == 0:
        reduced_log_dict = {
            f"{metric_name}/{key}": sum([d[key] for d in gathered_log_dict]) / pg.size for key in log_dict
        }
        logger.info(f"{metric_name} {rollout_id}: {reduced_log_dict}")

        # Calculate step once to avoid duplication
        step = compute_rollout_step(args, rollout_id)
        reduced_log_dict["rollout/step"] = step
        tracking.log(args, reduced_log_dict, step_key="rollout/step")

        return reduced_log_dict
    else:
        return None


def aggregate_forward_results(
    forward_data_store: list[dict[str, list]],
    data_iterator: DataIterator,
    args: Namespace,
    store_prefix: str = "",
) -> dict[str, list]:
    rollout_data = {}
    if not forward_data_store:
        return rollout_data

    keys = forward_data_store[0].keys()
    for key in keys:
        values = []
        for batch_result in forward_data_store:
            assert isinstance(batch_result[key], list), f"Expected list for key {key}, got {type(batch_result[key])}"
            values += batch_result[key]

        # Handle dynamic batch size: restore original order
        if args.use_dynamic_batch_size and hasattr(data_iterator, "micro_batch_indices"):
            origin_values = [None] * len(values)
            origin_indices = sum(data_iterator.micro_batch_indices, [])
            for value, origin_index in zip(values, origin_indices, strict=False):
                origin_values[origin_index] = value
            values = origin_values

        rollout_data[key] = values

    return rollout_data


def log_rollout_data(rollout_id: int, args: Namespace, rollout_data: RolloutBatch) -> None:
    """
    Summarize rollout fields and log reduced metrics on PP last stage, TP rank 0.

    - Tensor-valued lists are concatenated and averaged. For token-level metrics
      like log-probs/returns/advantages/values, computes a CP-correct sample mean
      using `loss_masks` and total/response lengths.
    - Non-tensor lists are averaged elementwise.
    - Scalars are converted to Python numbers.
    """
    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()
    if parallel_state.tp.rank == 0 and parallel_state.is_pp_last_stage:
        cp_size = parallel_state.cp.size
        log_dict = {}
        response_lengths = rollout_data["response_lengths"]
        loss_masks = rollout_data["loss_masks"]
        total_lengths = rollout_data["total_lengths"]
        max_seq_lens = rollout_data.get("max_seq_lens", None)

        for key, val in rollout_data.items():
            if key in [
                "tokens",
                "multimodal_train_inputs",
                "loss_masks",
                "sample_indices",
                "rollout_routed_experts",
                "rollout_indexer_topk",
                "max_seq_lens",
                "dynamic_global_batch_size",
                "witness_ids",
                "weight_versions",
                "metadata",
                "n_adapters",
                "adapter_slots",
                "step_slots",
                "step_adapter_names",
                "step_adapter_batch_sizes",
                "prompt_group_sizes",
            ]:
                continue
            # Upload per sample mean for each rollout value
            # There are the following assumptions:
            # - Each dp rank has the same number of samples
            if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)):
                if isinstance(val[0], torch.Tensor):
                    # NOTE: Here we have to do the clone().detach(), otherwise the tensor will be
                    # modified in place and will cause problem for the next rollout.
                    # reshape to 1-d before cat: a CP rank with exactly 1 response
                    # token produces a 0-d scalar that torch.cat rejects.
                    val = torch.cat([t.reshape(-1) for t in val]).clone().detach()
                    if val.device != loss_masks[0].device:
                        val = val.to(loss_masks[0].device)
                    if key in [
                        "log_probs",
                        "ref_log_probs",
                        "rollout_log_probs",
                        "returns",
                        "advantages",
                        "values",
                        "teacher_log_probs",
                        "opd_reverse_kl",
                        "entropy",
                    ]:
                        sum_of_sample_mean = get_sum_of_sample_mean(
                            total_lengths,
                            response_lengths,
                            loss_masks,
                            qkv_format=args.qkv_format,
                            max_seq_lens=max_seq_lens,
                        )
                        val = cp_size * sum_of_sample_mean(val) / len(loss_masks)
                    else:
                        val = val.mean() * cp_size

        step = compute_rollout_step(args, rollout_id)
        reduced_log_dict["rollout/step"] = step
        tracking.log(args, reduced_log_dict, step_key="rollout/step")

        return reduced_log_dict
    else:
        return None


def aggregate_forward_results(
    forward_data_store: list[dict[str, list]],
    data_iterator: DataIterator,
    args: Namespace,
    store_prefix: str = "",
) -> dict[str, list]:
    rollout_data = {}
    if not forward_data_store:
        return rollout_data

    keys = forward_data_store[0].keys()
    for key in keys:
        values = []
        for batch_result in forward_data_store:
            assert isinstance(batch_result[key], list), f"Expected list for key {key}, got {type(batch_result[key])}"
            values += batch_result[key]

        # Handle dynamic batch size: restore original order
        if args.use_dynamic_batch_size and hasattr(data_iterator, "micro_batch_indices"):
            origin_values = [None] * len(values)
            origin_indices = sum(data_iterator.micro_batch_indices, [])
            for value, origin_index in zip(values, origin_indices, strict=False):
                origin_values[origin_index] = value
            values = origin_values

        rollout_data[key] = values

    return rollout_data


def log_rollout_data(rollout_id: int, args: Namespace, rollout_data: RolloutBatch) -> None:
    """
    Summarize rollout fields and log reduced metrics on PP last stage, TP rank 0.

    - Tensor-valued lists are concatenated and averaged. For token-level metrics
      like log-probs/returns/advantages/values, computes a CP-correct sample mean
      using `loss_masks` and total/response lengths.
    - Non-tensor lists are averaged elementwise.
    - Scalars are converted to Python numbers.
    """
    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()
    if parallel_state.tp.rank == 0 and parallel_state.is_pp_last_stage:
        cp_size = parallel_state.cp.size
        log_dict = {}
        response_lengths = rollout_data["response_lengths"]
        loss_masks = rollout_data["loss_masks"]
        total_lengths = rollout_data["total_lengths"]
        max_seq_lens = rollout_data.get("max_seq_lens", None)

        for key, val in rollout_data.items():
            if key in [
                "tokens",
                "multimodal_train_inputs",
                "loss_masks",
                "sample_indices",
                "rollout_routed_experts",
                "rollout_indexer_topk",
                "max_seq_lens",
                "dynamic_global_batch_size",
                "witness_ids",
                "weight_versions",
                "metadata",
                "n_adapters",
                "adapter_slots",
                "step_slots",
                "step_adapter_names",
                "step_adapter_batch_sizes",
                "prompt_group_sizes",
            ]:
                continue
            # Upload per sample mean for each rollout value
            # There are the following assumptions:
            # - Each dp rank has the same number of samples
            if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)):
                if isinstance(val[0], torch.Tensor):
                    # NOTE: Here we have to do the clone().detach(), otherwise the tensor will be
                    # modified in place and will cause problem for the next rollout.
                    # reshape to 1-d before cat: a CP rank with exactly 1 response
                    # token produces a 0-d scalar that torch.cat rejects.
                    val = torch.cat([t.reshape(-1) for t in val]).clone().detach()
                    if val.device != loss_masks[0].device:
                        val = val.to(loss_masks[0].device)
                    if key in [
                        "log_probs",
                        "ref_log_probs",
                        "rollout_log_probs",
                        "returns",
                        "advantages",
                        "values",
                        "teacher_log_probs",
                        "opd_reverse_kl",
                        "entropy",
                    ]:
                        sum_of_sample_mean = get_sum_of_sample_mean(
                            total_lengths,
                            response_lengths,
                            loss_masks,
                            qkv_format=args.qkv_format,
                            max_seq_lens=max_seq_lens,
                        )
                        val = cp_size * sum_of_sample_mean(val) / len(loss_masks)
                    else:
                        val = val.mean() * cp_size

        )
        advantages = [r for r in returns]

    elif args.advantage_estimator == "reinforce_plus_plus_baseline":

from miles.backends.training_utils.parallel import get_parallel_state
from miles.utils.audit_utils.event_logger.logger import get_event_logger, is_event_logger_initialized
from miles.utils.audit_utils.event_logger.models import TrainAdvantageComputationEvent
from miles.utils.multi_lora import is_multi_lora_enabled
from miles.utils.types import RolloutBatch


def compute_advantages_and_returns(args: Namespace, rollout_data: RolloutBatch) -> None:
    """Compute advantages and returns in-place based on `args.advantage_estimator`.

    This function extracts rewards, log-probs, values, and masks from
    `rollout_data`, computes KL divergences, then applies the chosen advantage
    estimator. Supported methods: "grpo", "gspo", "ppo", "reinforce_plus_plus",
    and "reinforce_plus_plus_baseline". On-policy distillation (OPD) is applied
    orthogonally on top of any estimator via `args.use_opd`. When
    `args.normalize_advantages` is True, advantages are whitened across the
    data-parallel group using masked statistics.

    Early returns if both `log_probs` and `values` are None (intermediate
    pipeline stages).

    Args:
        args: Configuration specifying estimator type, KL coefficient,
            normalization settings, and other hyperparameters.
        rollout_data: Dict containing input lists ("log_probs", "ref_log_probs",
            "rewards", "values", "response_lengths", "loss_masks",
            "total_lengths"). Modified in-place to add "advantages" and
            "returns" keys, each mapping to lists of tensors per sample.
    """
    log_probs: list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("rollout_log_probs" if args.use_rollout_logprobs else "log_probs")
    ref_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("ref_log_probs")
    rewards: list[float] = rollout_data.get("rewards")
    values: None | list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("values")
    response_lengths: list[int] = rollout_data.get("response_lengths")
    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("loss_masks")
    total_lengths: list[int] = rollout_data.get("total_lengths")
    max_seq_lens: list[int] | None = rollout_data.get("max_seq_lens", None)

    # return when not the last pp stage.
    if log_probs is None and values is None:
        return

    if args.kl_coef == 0 or not log_probs:
        # when kl_coef is 0, we won't compute ref_log_prob
        xs = log_probs if log_probs is not None else values
        kl = [torch.zeros_like(x, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device) for x in xs]
    else:
        kl = [
            compute_approx_kl(
                log_probs[i],
                ref_log_probs[i],
                kl_loss_type=args.kl_loss_type,
            )
            for i in range(len(log_probs))
        ]

    advantages, returns = compute_advantages(
        args=args,
        kl=kl,
        rewards=rewards,
        log_probs=log_probs,
        loss_masks=loss_masks,
        total_lengths=total_lengths,
        response_lengths=response_lengths,
        max_seq_lens=max_seq_lens,
        values=values,
    )

    # Apply on-policy distillation KL penalty to advantages (orthogonal to advantage estimator)
    if args.use_opd:
        apply_opd_kl_to_advantages(
            args=args,
            rollout_data=rollout_data,
            advantages=advantages,
            student_log_probs=log_probs,
        )

    if args.normalize_advantages:
        advantages = normalize_advantages(args, advantages, loss_masks, total_lengths, response_lengths, max_seq_lens)

    rollout_data["advantages"] = advantages
    rollout_data["returns"] = returns

import asyncio
import logging

from miles.ray.placement_group import create_placement_groups, create_rollout_manager, create_training_models
from miles.utils.arguments import parse_args
from miles.utils.async_utils import eager_create_task
from miles.utils.audit_utils.process_identity import MainProcessIdentity
from miles.utils.debug_utils.periodic_py_spy import maybe_start_periodic_pyspy_dump
from miles.utils.ft_utils.control_server.server import start_control_server
from miles.utils.ft_utils.mini_ft_controller import maybe_start_mini_ft_controller
from miles.utils.logging_utils import configure_logger
from miles.utils.misc import should_run_periodic_action
from miles.utils.tracking_utils.tracking import finish_tracking, init_tracking

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# The framework supports other asynchronous approaches such as fully async (which is shown in examples/full_async).
async def train(args):
    assert not args.colocate, "Colocation is not supported for async training."
    configure_logger(args, source=MainProcessIdentity())
    maybe_start_periodic_pyspy_dump()
    # allocate the GPUs
    pgs = create_placement_groups(args)
    init_tracking(args)

    # create the rollout manager, with sglang engines inside.
    # need to initialize rollout manager first to calculate num_rollout
    rollout_manager, num_rollout_per_epoch = create_rollout_manager(args, pgs["rollout"])

    # create the actor and critic models
    actor_model, critic_model = await create_training_models(args, pgs, rollout_manager)

    if args.control_server_port:
        start_control_server(
            actor_model=actor_model,
            rollout_manager=rollout_manager,
            port=args.control_server_port,
            ft_components=args.ft_components,
        )

    maybe_start_mini_ft_controller(args)

    # always update weight first so that sglang has the loaded weights from training.
    await actor_model.update_weights()

    if args.check_weight_update_equal:
        await rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(
            action="compare",
            allow_quant_error=args.check_weight_update_allow_quant_error,
            selector=args.check_weight_update_selector,
            skip_list=args.check_weight_update_skip_list,
        )

    if args.eval_interval is not None and args.start_rollout_id == 0 and not args.skip_eval_before_train:
        await rollout_manager.eval.remote(0)

    # async train loop.
    rollout_data_next_future = rollout_manager.generate.remote(args.start_rollout_id)
    for rollout_id in range(args.start_rollout_id, args.num_rollout):
        # Sync the last generation
        if rollout_data_next_future is not None:
            rollout_data_curr_ref = await rollout_data_next_future

        # Start the next rollout early.
        if rollout_id + 1 < args.num_rollout:
            rollout_data_next_future = rollout_manager.generate.remote(rollout_id + 1)

        if args.use_critic:
            critic_task = await eager_create_task(critic_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_curr_ref))
            if rollout_id >= args.num_critic_only_steps:
                await actor_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_curr_ref)
            await critic_task
        else:
            await actor_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_curr_ref)

        if should_run_periodic_action(rollout_id, args.save_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch, args.num_rollout):
            await actor_model.save_model(
                rollout_id,
                force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
            )
            if args.use_critic:
                await critic_model.save_model(
                    rollout_id,
                    force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
                )
            await rollout_manager.save.remote(rollout_id)

        if (rollout_id + 1) % args.update_weights_interval == 0:
            # sync generate before update weights to prevent update weight in the middle of generation
            rollout_data_curr_ref = (await x) if (x := rollout_data_next_future) is not None else None
            rollout_data_next_future = None
            await actor_model.update_weights(rollout_id=rollout_id)

        if should_run_periodic_action(rollout_id, args.eval_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch):
            await rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id)

        if (
            args.debug_exit_after_rollout is not None
            and (rollout_id - args.start_rollout_id + 1) >= args.debug_exit_after_rollout
        ):
            logger.info(
                "debug_exit_after_rollout=%d reached at rollout_id=%d, exiting",
                args.debug_exit_after_rollout,
                rollout_id,
            )
            break

    await rollout_manager.dispose.remote()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()
    try:
        asyncio.run(train(args))
    finally:
        finish_tracking()

import os
import runpy
from pathlib import Path

FORWARDED = ["PYTHONPATH", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE", "NO_VCS_VERSION", "TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM",

             "HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE"]


def main():
    import ray
    import torch

    workspace = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

    env_vars = {name: os.environ[name] for name in FORWARDED + extra if name in os.environ}
    gpus = torch.cuda.device_count()
    ray.init(address="local", num_gpus=gpus, num_cpus=max(16, gpus * 8), include_dashboard=False,
             log_to_driver=True, runtime_env={"env_vars": env_vars})

import asyncio
import logging

from miles.ray.placement_group import create_placement_groups, create_rollout_manager, create_training_models
from miles.utils.arguments import parse_args
from miles.utils.async_utils import eager_create_task
from miles.utils.audit_utils.process_identity import MainProcessIdentity
from miles.utils.debug_utils.periodic_py_spy import maybe_start_periodic_pyspy_dump
from miles.utils.ft_utils.control_server.server import start_control_server
from miles.utils.ft_utils.mini_ft_controller import maybe_start_mini_ft_controller
from miles.utils.logging_utils import configure_logger
from miles.utils.misc import should_run_periodic_action
from miles.utils.tracking_utils.tracking import finish_tracking, init_tracking

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# The framework supports other asynchronous approaches such as fully async (which is shown in examples/full_async).
async def train(args):
    assert not args.colocate, "Colocation is not supported for async training."
    configure_logger(args, source=MainProcessIdentity())
    maybe_start_periodic_pyspy_dump()
    # allocate the GPUs
    pgs = create_placement_groups(args)
    init_tracking(args)

    # create the rollout manager, with sglang engines inside.
    # need to initialize rollout manager first to calculate num_rollout
    rollout_manager, num_rollout_per_epoch = create_rollout_manager(args, pgs["rollout"])

    # create the actor and critic models
    actor_model, critic_model = await create_training_models(args, pgs, rollout_manager)

    if args.control_server_port:
        start_control_server(
            actor_model=actor_model,
            rollout_manager=rollout_manager,
            port=args.control_server_port,
            ft_components=args.ft_components,
        )

    maybe_start_mini_ft_controller(args)

    # always update weight first so that sglang has the loaded weights from training.
    await actor_model.update_weights()

    if args.check_weight_update_equal:
        await rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(
            action="compare",
            allow_quant_error=args.check_weight_update_allow_quant_error,
            selector=args.check_weight_update_selector,
            skip_list=args.check_weight_update_skip_list,
        )

    if args.eval_interval is not None and args.start_rollout_id == 0 and not args.skip_eval_before_train:
        await rollout_manager.eval.remote(0)

    # async train loop.
    rollout_data_next_future = rollout_manager.generate.remote(args.start_rollout_id)
    for rollout_id in range(args.start_rollout_id, args.num_rollout):
        # Sync the last generation
        if rollout_data_next_future is not None:
            rollout_data_curr_ref = await rollout_data_next_future

        # Start the next rollout early.
        if rollout_id + 1 < args.num_rollout:
            rollout_data_next_future = rollout_manager.generate.remote(rollout_id + 1)

        if args.use_critic:
            critic_task = await eager_create_task(critic_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_curr_ref))
            if rollout_id >= args.num_critic_only_steps:
                await actor_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_curr_ref)
            await critic_task
        else:
            await actor_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_curr_ref)

        if should_run_periodic_action(rollout_id, args.save_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch, args.num_rollout):
            await actor_model.save_model(
                rollout_id,
                force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
            )
            if args.use_critic:
                await critic_model.save_model(
                    rollout_id,
                    force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
                )
            await rollout_manager.save.remote(rollout_id)

        if (rollout_id + 1) % args.update_weights_interval == 0:
            # sync generate before update weights to prevent update weight in the middle of generation
            rollout_data_curr_ref = (await x) if (x := rollout_data_next_future) is not None else None
            rollout_data_next_future = None
            await actor_model.update_weights(rollout_id=rollout_id)

        if should_run_periodic_action(rollout_id, args.eval_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch):
            await rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id)

        if (
            args.debug_exit_after_rollout is not None
            and (rollout_id - args.start_rollout_id + 1) >= args.debug_exit_after_rollout
        ):
            logger.info(
                "debug_exit_after_rollout=%d reached at rollout_id=%d, exiting",
                args.debug_exit_after_rollout,
                rollout_id,
            )
            break

    await rollout_manager.dispose.remote()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()
    try:
        asyncio.run(train(args))
    finally:
        finish_tracking()


So at each iteration, it starts the *next* rollout generation, trains on current data, then awaits the next rollout to finish before updating weights, and sets next=None. This means generation for rollout id+1 completes before weight update for step id. So rollout id+1 data is generated with weights from before step id, i.e., stale by one step. That's by design of this "sync before update" pattern. Then next iteration uses that already-generated rollout data, starts rollout id+2, trains, waits, updates. So rollout id+2 is generated *after* the weight update from step id... Wait, careful.

Sequence with num_rollout=3:
- Initially, future = generate(0).
- iter 0: await generate(0) → data0 (version 1 initial weights). start generate(1). train(0). Then since (0+1)%1==0: await future = generate(1) → data1; future=None; update_weights(0) [version 2].
- iter 1: curr_ref = await future → but future is None! `rollout_data_curr_ref = await rollout_data_next_future` where rollout_data_next_future is None → `await None` would error! Wait: at end of iter 0, they set rollout_data_next_future=None. At start of iter 1, `if rollout_data_next_future is not None: rollout_data_curr_ref = await rollout_data_next_future`. Let me re-read:

```
    rollout_data_next_future = rollout_manager.generate.remote(args.start_rollout_id)
    for rollout_id in range(args.start_rollout_id, args.num_rollout):
        # Sync the last generation

        # Start the next rollout early.
        if rollout_id + 1 < args.num_rollout:
            rollout_data_next_future = rollout_manager.generate.remote(rollout_id + 1)
        ...
```

Right, there's an `if is not None`. In iter 1: future is None → rollout_data_curr_ref remains the value from the update block (data1). Then start generate(2). train(1) on data1. Then update block awaits generate(2) → data2; updates weights (step1). iter 2: future None → curr_ref = data2; train(2); update block: (2+1)%1==0 → future is None → curr_ref = None; update_weights(2).

So the sequence is: all generation for rollout N+1 happens *during* training of rollout N, and the trainer waits for it before updating weights. The data for step N+1 is generated with weights from step N-1 (or initial for step 0/1). Because update_weights(N) happens after generation(N+1) completes. So data for step 1 and step 2 are both generated with initial weights (version 1), since the first update_weights only happens after generate(1) at 08:42:30. Exactly what we observed: all 3 rollouts have weight_version 1.

This is by design in `train_async_entrypoint.py`: "sync generate before update weights to prevent update weight in the middle of generation". So this "async training" is really off-policy by 2 steps: rollout N+1 generated with weights from step N-1. With update_weights_interval=1. That's an implementation choice. `train_async_entrypoint.py` is the Miles asynchronous training driver that
`scripts/native_entrypoint.py` executes inside a local Ray cluster. It creates
the rollout manager (SGLang engines and router), the Megatron actor, performs
the initial weight sync, and then overlaps rollout `k+1` with training on
rollout `k`, syncing weights after every update.

| Location | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `train_async_entrypoint.py` | Miles `train_async.py` driver |
| `../fully_async.py`, `../progress_watchdog.py` | continuous rollout producer used by the original runs, generic parts only |
| `../../vendor/miles/`, `../../vendor/miles_plugins/` | Miles `0.2.1.dev1609+g48f39cb4` Python source |
| `../../vendor/megatron/` | Megatron-Core `0.18.0+caeabd765` and Megatron-Bridge `0.5.0` Python source |
| `../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `../../licenses/` | ownership and license notices |

Compiled dependencies (CUDA, Transformer Engine, FlashAttention, SGLang
kernels) come from the task image; bundled Python source takes precedence on
`PYTHONPATH`.

steps.reasoning_content:
The README says: "overlaps rollout k+1 with training on rollout k, syncing weights after every update." That's the design. It doesn't say rollout k+1 uses weights after update k. Actually in standard async training, you would update weights as soon as training step k finishes, while rollout k+1 is in flight; the in-flight rollout continues with old weights (off-policy). Here, the driver *waits* for rollout k+1 to finish before updating weights, which makes rollout k+1 100% generated with pre-step-k weights. This creates a fixed one-step lag but avoids aborts. Given update_weights_interval=1 and pause mode abort, this design means every batch is generated by the previous policy, which is normal-ish for async (off-policy by 1). But because of the initial prefetch, all 3 rollouts version 1. With more rollouts, version would advance? Let's simulate: update_weights(0) after generate(1) → version 2. Then iter1 starts generate(2) at the *beginning* of iter 1, but at that point update_weights(0) has just completed. So generate(2) uses version 2. Then train(1) with data1 (version 1). Then wait generate(2) (version 2), update_weights(1) → version 3. So each step trains on data generated one weight version behind — standard one-step off-policy. With num_rollout=3: data0 v1, data1 v1, data2 v2. But observed rollout 2 weight_version 1.0, not 2! Why?

Wait, rollout 2's data was collected at 08:42:30 — the *same moment* as update_weights(0) finished (08:42:30.569). Hmm. Let's re-check the driver loop: iter0 starts generate(0) before loop; then in iter0, generate(1) starts at 08:38:12; then train(0) until 08:42:29; then update block: await generate(1) → but generate(1) already finished at 08:39:29 (recorded). Then update_weights(0) at 08:42:29-08:42:30. Then iter1: future is None; curr_ref = data1; starts generate(2) at 08:42:30.572 — immediately after update_weights(0) completed at 08:42:30.569. So generate(2) starts *after* weight update → should be version 2. But the rollout 2 samples show weight_version 1.0! Because the generate(2) call returns 16 groups taken from the *producer's queue*, which were generated long before (during training). The producer's persistent queue means "generate(2)" doesn't generate; it consumes stale queued groups. So the driver's "wait for generation then update weights" safeguard is defeated by the persistent producer that has already generated the next batch(es) ahead of time. That is a real architectural mismatch: the outer driver assumes generate(k+1) happens during training(k) and completes with pre-update weights; but the inner producer runs ahead by up to 2 batches, so by the time a new rollout is requested, its data is old, and weight versions don't advance.

But even with 1-batch prefetch: at iter0 generate(1) called at 08:38:12; the producer has been running since 08:34:17 with max_inflight 32 and queue 32. It had already completed 16 groups at 08:38:12 (queue_size 0? At rollout 0 complete, producer completed=16, active=32, fetched=48: it had generated 16 and had 32 active). generate(1) then consumes the queued 16 (completed groups 16-31?) Hmm, at the time generate(1) starts, producer had completed exactly 16 (consumed by rollout 0) and active 32. So generate(1) must wait for new completions; those arrive between 08:38:12 and 08:39:29 — still version 1 (pre-update). Then generate(2) at 08:42:30: the producer had generated 63 completions, of which 16+16=32 consumed... wait completed=63 at rollout 2 start; rollout 0 and 1 consumed 16 each; queue_size 31. So 15 more completed after... Actually 63 - 32 consumed = 31 queued. Good.

Anyway, the queued groups for rollout 2 were generated between 08:39:29 and 08:42:27 (version 1). So version 1. If the producer had been bounded to exactly 16 in-flight and 16 queue, then rollout 2's 16 groups would have been generated after... hmm, after generate(1) consumed the queue at 08:38-08:39, the producer would start generating more; at 08:39:29 it would have 16 in-flight; those would complete by ~08:41 and be queued; then at 08:42:30 generate(2) would consume them (version 1). So still version 1. To get version 2 for rollout 2, the producer must be stopped from running ahead once a batch is queued — e.g., queue maxsize = 0 blocks until consumer takes them (but then producer generation is not overlapped? It would still fill the queue of 16 as they complete). Hmm, with num_rollout=3 and one-batch overlap, the data for step 2 is necessarily generated during step 0's long training, before update 0. So the driver's design "generate k+1 during train k, then update" means step k+1 always trains on pre-step-k weights. So with 3 steps, all 3 use v1. This is inherent to this sync-before-update design + initial weights + slow training. It's not a "bug" per se, but a poor setup: the model effectively never trains on its own updated outputs within this run. With only 3 rollouts, no learning can be observed. The public rerun is a "reproduction" that ends after 3 rollouts; maybe that's intended for verification.

Hmm. Let's step back and search for more concrete issues in the code. The task says "find the concrete root cause or causes in the code and configuration". So there likely are actual bugs. Let's examine runtime/training_evidence.py for correctness: it patches optimizer.step and snapshots params. `picked = [i for i in range(0, len(params), 16) if ...]`. Params = all trainable tensors across chunks. It writes delta. Looks fine.

But wait: `trainer_code = inspect.unwrap(trainer_module.train_one_step).__code__`, then `called_from_trainer()` checks frames for that code. But `model.train_one_step` may be decorated; inspect.unwrap gets the wrapped function. `called_from_trainer: true`. Fine.

Now `observe_train_step(args, rollout_id, step_id, model, optimizer, opt_param_scheduler)` is invoked as before-train-step hook. It sets `optimizer._evidence_identity = (rollout_id, step_id)` and then wraps optimizer.step once. But the hook is called every step; `if hasattr(optimizer, "_evidence_original_step"): return` — good, it returns early after first call, but it *does* update `_evidence_identity` before the check. Good.

Now, `optimizer.step` returns (success, grad_norm, num_zeros). Fine.

Potential issue: rank 0-3 writes step.X.0.rankR.json. In the logs, some ranks printed duplicate evidence lines (rank1 at 08:43:13, rank2 etc.). The `rollout_id` in the evidence corresponds to the train step; good.

Now, is there any mismatch between rollout_id in evidence and the data? Step 0 evidence t=08:42:28, step 1 t=08:43:13, step 2 t=08:43:51.

Let's examine `runtime/rollout.py` `_flatten`: 
```
for group in groups:
    for item in group:
        if isinstance(item, list): yield from item
        else: yield item
```
Fine.

Now `_summary`: `cached = sum(s.prefix_cache_info.cached_tokens ...)`, `prompt = sum(s.prefix_cache_info.total_prompt_tokens ...)`. Prefix cache 66%.

The `engine_prompt_tokens` 865871 over 128 samples = 6765 tokens per sample; per-turn prompt tokens ~ 604+734+965+1162+2273+3571+4544+5447 = 19,300 total per trajectory across turns (sum). 128 × ~6765 = 865,920. Yes, matches. So per-turn prompt tokens counted repeatedly. Fine.

Now let's compute the proportion of prompt tokens that are cached: 66%. That's decent.

So what's unhealthy? Let's enumerate suspicious evidence:
1. Sandbox setup semaphore waits p50 35s / p90 115s / max 160s; create_s p50 18.8s; 662 setups for 384 consumed trajectories. This delays rollout and wastes capacity.
2. 131 sandboxes leaked at shutdown (678 creates vs 547 deletes). The shutdown path didn't clean up because is_last_rollout stops the producer while 32 groups are in flight/queued; "drained 15 completed and 0 retry groups".
3. All 3 training batches have weight_version 1.0; no update is reflected in the rollout data. The reward trend is flat (0.92→0.81→0.90) and high; 50-56% of groups are all-correct → zero GRPO advantage.
4. The output queue prefetch means rollout 2's "rollout_time" is 3.2s; the reported rollout metrics are misleading (perf tokens/gpu/sec 30570) and rollout attribution is wrong: the batch consumed for rollout 2 was generated during rollout 1. But that's inherent.

5. The biggest health issue might be the sandbox setup bottleneck: `MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP` default 32 and `SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY` 32 vs `PUBLIC_ASYNC_MAX_INFLIGHT_GROUPS=32 groups × 8 samples = 256 trajectories`. Each setup holds a slot through create+upload+install (median 3.9s tool_setup + create 18.8s = ~23s) → only ~1.4 setups/s; 256 setups need ~180s. This matches rollout 0 taking 234s and semaphore waits of 160s. And historical runs with 8 engines/32 groups showed even worse (190-450s waits). So the root cause: concurrency mismatch — in-flight trajectories far exceed sandbox setup slots. But is this "the training setup is unhealthy"? It slows rollouts, but rollout is not the bottleneck here: training step takes 42s while rollouts overlap. Actually the first train_wait is 367.7s because the initial rollout took 234s and init took time. The `wait_time_ratio` 0.59 for step 0. The 3-step run total wall ~14 min, of which ~6 min is waiting for rollout 0 + initial setup.

6. `sandbox_service.log` empty, but that's not an issue.

Let's look for configuration errors like data duplication: `--rollout-shuffle --rollout-seed 20261116`. Data source may sample with replacement or iterate epochs. Let's check data_source.py in Miles. If the same task appears in multiple groups across rollouts, that's fine.

Maybe the key bug is with `num_rollout` semantics: `--num-rollout 3` means 3 rollouts × 16 groups × 8 samples = 384 samples. The producer fetched 95 groups (760 samples) because it kept running ahead; 15 completed groups were drained and discarded at shutdown. That's ~40% wasted rollout compute and 131 leaked sandboxes. A "healthy" fully-async setup should stop fetching when enough groups for the remaining rollouts are queued. But the producer doesn't know how many rollouts remain; `_is_last_rollout` stops at the start of the last rollout, dropping queued work. That's by design, though wasteful.

Let's look at the historical logs more concretely. Maybe they contain a critical clue about what's expected: e.g., specific error messages "weight version", "stale", "0 accepted", "sandbox" etc. Let's extract message type counts and interesting lines from run-a/run-b.

EOF

Established running hypotheses and evidence:
- **Root cause candidate A — pipeline oversubscription / staleness:** `PUBLIC_ASYNC_MAX_INFLIGHT_GROUPS=32` and `PUBLIC_ASYNC_QUEUE_MAXSIZE=32` with `rollout_batch_size=16` make the persistent producer run 2 batches ahead (vs historical 32/32 with 32 groups). `runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py` waits for rollout k+1 before `update_weights(k)`, so all measured training batches were generated before the first weight update. Evidence: `rollout/weight_version` mean/median/max/min = 1.0 and `mixed_version_ratio=0.0` for all three rollouts; first update_weights to engines at 08:42:30, after rollout 2 was already queued (queue_size 31; rollout 2 completes in 0.0 s at 08:42:30.571); optimizer steps at 08:42:28.985/08:43:13.107/08:43:51.874; reward flat 0.9219→0.8125→0.8984. `max_weight_staleness` is None (no stale-group recycling).
- **Root cause candidate B — sandbox setup concurrency:** `MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP` default 32 (`vendor/agent_runtime/env_runtime.py`) vs 32 groups × 8 = 256 in-flight trajectories; the semaphore is held across create (service median 6 s, client-observed p50 18.8 s due to contention) + upload + install; sem waits p50 35.5 s / p90 114.7 s / max 160 s; 662 setups for 384 consumed samples; rollout 0 234.8 s and initial train_wait 367.7 s. Historical runs show the same pathology worse (sem p50 ~190–205 s; ~8–13 running requests across 8 engines; run-b slow generate max 3349 s).
- **Root cause candidate C — insufficient optimization signal:** task generator leaks the target in `test_failure` (`tests/test_<module>.py::test_<fn>`), and user prompt names the domain; solve rate 0.81–0.92, rewards only 0/1; 50–56% of groups all-correct → zero GRPO advantage (`zero_std/count_1.0` 9/6/8 of 16; `all_one_percentage` 0.5625/0.375/0.5). `dynamic_sampling_filter_path=None` in this run so zero-std groups are kept (historical run-b had a dynamic filter and dropped solve_all/solve_none/insufficient_scored_samples groups). Note `train/loss ≈ 0` is normal GRPO behavior, not evidence of a broken optimizer; grad norms and parameter deltas confirm updates occurred.
- **Symptom/waste candidate D:** producer ran far ahead; on last rollout stop, 15 completed groups drained and discarded, 32 active tasks cancelled, 131 sandboxes leaked (create 678 vs delete 547, live 131); rollout 2 wall 3.2 s and 30,570 tokens/GPU/s are artifacts of consuming pre-generated queue data.

steps.reasoning_content:
This is very revealing: even at the very start of the run (08:34:26–30), the engines have only 1–5 running requests and queue 0. The producer has 32 groups = 256 trajectories. Yet only ~1-5 requests per engine. So the bottleneck is definitely upstream of the engines: trajectories are spending almost all their time in sandbox setup/tool calls/agent loop, not LLM generation. The engines are massively underutilized (4 engines × ~2 running requests). `gen throughput 50–550 token/s` — low.

This is strong evidence for the sandbox setup bottleneck: during rollout 0, from 08:34:26 to 08:38:12, the engines are mostly idle with 0-5 requests. 256 trajectories but only ~4-10 in generation at a time. Why? Because each trajectory must first acquire the setup semaphore (32 slots) and wait 35-160 s; then each turn is a quick 1-2 s generate, then a tool call (exec 0.4 s), then next generate. Hmm, but with 256 trajectories, once setup is done, there should be many generate calls. Unless the semaphore is held for the entire *session* rather than just setup? Let me check `env_runtime.py`: the summary says "holds semaphore across create+upload+install" — only setup. After setup, the semaphore is released. So all 256 trajectories eventually get set up and then should generate. But observed only 1-5 running per engine. Maybe because the 32-slot semaphore creates waves: 32 sessions set up, do a few turns quickly, then finish; next 32...
